items.rationale: The indoor heating-pipe repair falls under §2.4.3(a). Under §§7.1.5 and 7.1.9, the allowance is limited to plain copper for the repaired section, benchmarked at 6.4 m × €15 gross, with no chrome premium.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.9 allow the standard fittings needed for the repair, not the designer finish. Case 40 supports about €10.50 each, or €42 for four.
Under §§7.1.7(c) and 7.1.9, the allowance is for ordinary copper fittings used in the repaired section. Using Case 40, five at €21 gross gives €105.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.9 limit this to the price of one standard copper elbow, estimated at €21 gross from Case 40.
Minor fixings are allowed under §§7.1.7(c) and 7.1.8(e). Case 40 puts the same eight-screw line at €7–€10 gross.

Section 7.1.8(e) excludes material whose dimensions do not correspond to the documented repair; no 10 mm pipe or use for these clamps is shown. If their use is substantiated, four standard clamps at €4.50 would total €18 gross.
Standard supports attributable to the repaired run are allowed under §7.1.7(c). Case 40 supports about €6.25 each, or €25 gross for four.

Sections 7.1.7(g) and 7.1.9 allow ordinary repair labour but not extra time for the new devices or premium installation. At about €90 gross per hour using Case 40, allowing roughly six of the 6.75 billed hours gives €540.
Sections 7.1.7(g) and 7.1.9 allow helper time for the standard repair only. Allowing about five of the 5.75 billed hours at €68 gross per hour, calibrated to Case 40, gives €340.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.9 limit the allowance to the pre-loss rock-wool specification. Six equivalent shells at about €20 gross each give €120, consistent with Case 40.
Section 7.1.7(c) allows repair consumables to the extent attributable to the work. Case 40 supports about €10 per kg, or €20 gross for 2 kg, if the billed wire was used for the repair.
Section 7.1.9 excludes installations not present before the loss. The €85 conditional figure is for one sensor only and is not an allowance for this new addition.
Section 7.1.9 excludes the valve because it was not part of the pre-loss installation. The €115 conditional figure is for one valve only and is not an allowance for this new addition.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.8(e) permit a lump sum for minor repair materials, excluding anything attributable solely to the upgrades. Case 40 supports about €35 gross for the repair allowance.
Section 7.1.7(f) permits the first travel charge per contractor per invoice. One trip is allowed at €75 gross, consistent with Case 40.
Sections 5.2.1 and 7.1.7(a) allow disposal of pipe and insulation removed for the covered repair. Case 40 supports €60 gross for one comparable disposal charge.
Section 7.1.8(b) expressly excludes administrative or processing fees charged on top of itemised labour and materials. The €20 conditional estimate for one fee is not payable under that clause.
